body:
## Summary
Six automation commands (screen, outreach, rejection, prep, scorecard, offer) look the entry's job up in the committed demo seed file instead of the role the app holds. Every role a team authors in-app answers `404 job not found`, and every seeded role is drafted from its seed copy - the offer letter for job-000 is priced from a 103000-154500 band while the board shows 110000-165000. Make the TS seam hand Python the entry's own job record (`--job-json`), resolve it through one `_cli.resolve_job_arg` door that the three per-job CLIs share, and key the prompt cache on the job bytes.

## Description
The engine has two planes: the demo seed (`data/seed_jobs/jobs.normalized.json`) and the live `jobs` table. rematch was moved onto the live plane (automation-run.ts:333-349), and the job-level interview kit reads a handed-in record (automation_cli.py:194-206), but the six per-entry commands still call `load_corpus(None)` (automation_cli.py:244) and `_find_job` (:93-99). On the operator DB, 5 of 105 jobs are in-app roles absent from the seed (`jd-*`), and 79 of the seeded ones carry a different salaryBand in the DB than in the seed file. The fix is structural rather than a flag: (1) `_cli.resolve_job_arg(job_id, job_json, jobs, jobs_json)` returns ONE Job - the handed record when present (id must match, else invalid_input), else the corpus lookup (not_found) - and automation_cli, recruiter_cli and winnability_cli call it instead of three hand-rolled lookups; (2) runAutomationTask serializes `getJob(entry.jobId, workspaceId)` once, writes it as job.json, pushes `--job-json`, and folds the same bytes into computeAutomationCacheKey as a `jobJson` axis (serialize-once, the profileJson/githubEvidenceJson pattern), so an in-app JD edit re-drafts instead of serving a 168h-stale screen. A deleted job row keeps today's `--job-id`-only path - no new refusal, no catalog entry. Read->write strategy: none needed - the run reads the job once and writes only the prompt cache keyed by those exact bytes, so a mid-spawn edit can only produce an entry keyed to the content it was drafted from. Perf: zero new TS modules (getJob comes from ./db/jobs, already imported); the task-hub graph is unchanged. Cost named: the new key axis retires the whole automation cache once, so warm entries re-draft (paid) on their next run - the same trade prior axis additions accepted.

## Flow
1. Write the eight acceptance cases (Python unittest + node:test) against the current tree - all red.
2. Add `resolve_job_arg` to `_cli.py`; switch automation_cli (six per-entry commands plus interview-kit's inline validate), recruiter_cli and winnability_cli onto it; add `--job-json` to automation_cli; delete `_find_job`.
3. In automation-run.ts extract the argv builder as an exported pure function, read the job record once, write job.json, push `--job-json`; correct the comment at :340.
4. Add the `jobJson` axis to AutomationKeyInput + computeAutomationCacheKey (gated off for rematch).
5. Update docs/features/pipeline/README.md: automation reads the entry's own job record; the seed file is the direct-CLI fallback only.
6. Gates: tsc, lint, test:unit, test:python:gate, docs:check.

## Expected impact
Every automation task on an in-app role stops failing: bulk AI screening, outreach, interview prep, the post-interview (voice) scorecard, the rejection letter and the offer draft all work on roles the team actually created - today none of them can. Offer letters price from the band the recruiter sees, and a JD edit re-keys the cache instead of serving a stale verdict for a week. One job door replaces three lookup shapes, so the next per-job CLI inherits the live plane by default.

## Evaluation
Claim: per-entry automation drafts against the entry's own job record, through one resolution door, with the job bytes as a cache axis.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - Python unittest cases in test_cli_job_resolution.py / test_automation_cli.py (CLI main() with temp files) and node:test cases in automation-cache-key.test.ts / automation-job-arg.test.ts, run under test:python:gate and test:unit.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract

title: Policy pass decides by stage role, not the five shipped stage names
acceptance: evaluate_entry({stage:'Inbox', stageRole:'entry', advanceTo:'Phone', matchScore:72, archetype:'bau'}) -> action 'advance', toStage 'Phone' (today: action 'none', reason 'no policy for this stage').

evaluate_entry({stage:'Tech screen', stageRole:'screening', advanceTo:'Panel', matchScore:30, archetype:'bau'}) -> action 'reject' (the single legal path, now resolved by role); the same entry with an early-career archetype -> 'hold'; with matchScore null -> 'hold' (never reject).

evaluate_entry({stage:'Tech screen', stageRole:'screening', advanceTo:'Panel', matchScore:80, daysInStage:3, archetype:'bau'}) -> action 'advance', toStage 'Panel', and the reason names 'Panel', not the literal 'Interview'.
stageRole in {'homework','scoring','custom','interview','offer'} -> 'hold' with a role-named reason; 'terminal' -> 'none'; never 'advance' or 'reject'.
stageRole null (a retired or off-axis column) -> action 'none', reason 'off-axis stage; no policy', never 'reject'.
No stageRole key (the bare CLI / back-compat): the existing PolicyTest fixtures for Accepted/Screened/Interview/Offer/Hired return byte-identical decisions (action, toStage, reason) to today.

TS: the exported `withPolicyStageFacts(entries, axisFor)` over the axis [Inbox:entry, Phone:screening, Panel:interview, Signed:terminal] stamps Inbox -> {stageRole:'entry', advanceTo:'Phone'}, Signed -> {stageRole:'terminal', advanceTo:null}, and an entry on retired 'Offer' -> {stageRole:null, advanceTo:null}; advanceTo always equals nextStageOnAxis(stage, axis), i.e. where actOnPipelineEntry('accept') will land.

Sync pin (the AgingTierSyncTest shape): Python's DEFAULT_STAGE_ROLE equals the STAGE_ROLE literal in app/_lib/pipeline-stages.ts, and Python's role vocabulary equals the StageRole union there - drift on either side fails test_automation.py.
premise: pipeline/jobfit/automation.py:951, :960, :980, :982, :987 - evaluate_entry branches on the literal names 'Accepted', 'Screened', 'Interview', 'Offer', 'Hired'; :989 answers `out("none", None, "no policy for this stage")` for anything else.
pipeline/jobfit/automation.py:958 and :977 - the advance targets are the literals 'Screened' and 'Interview'; :180 `TERMINAL_STAGES = ("Hired",)` guards the aging fallback by name.

app/_lib/decision-config-schema.ts:341-349 - a workspace axis may carry any stage ids with roles from ['entry','screening','homework','interview','scoring','offer','terminal','custom']; screening/homework/interview/custom repeat freely.

app/_lib/pipeline-axis-server.test.ts:39-48 - the axis tests themselves use a renamed board (Inbox:entry, Signed:terminal); app/_lib/pipeline-axis-server.ts:20-27 documents the same rename bug already fixed for writers.

app/_lib/automation-pass.ts:468 - the commit advances with `actOnPipelineEntry(d.entryId, "accept", ...)`, which lands on `nextStageOnAxis(row.stage, axis)` (app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3328; app/_lib/db/pipeline-core.ts:188) - not on Python's literal toStage, so on a renamed board the preview's planned stage and the landing stage differ.
app/_lib/automation-commit-plan.ts:71 - the preview/commit selection compares `kept.toStage` with `d.toStage` for advances, so the literal toStage is load-bearing in the drift check.
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:2921-2922 - the pass snapshot already resolves each entry's axis per workspace (for agingTier) but hands Python only the raw stage id.
pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_automation.py:148-160 - AgingTierSyncTest already reads app/_lib/pipeline-stages.ts from Python, the drift-guard shape this card reuses.
rollback: Two commits revert cleanly: the TS stamp is additive fields on the entries.json snapshot, and evaluate_entry falls back to the shipped name->role map whenever `stageRole` is absent, so reverting the TS commit alone restores today's decisions exactly.
runner_up: seed_interview_calendar.py:112-124 backfills calendar approvals across EVERY tenant with a bare SELECT then UPDATE on the literal 'Interview' stage - scope it to one workspace, resolve the interview role, and re-assert `approval_kind IS NULL` in the UPDATE's WHERE.

body:
## Summary
The deterministic policy pass (`evaluate_entry`) matches five shipped stage NAMES, while a workspace may compose its own board with any ids and roles. On a custom board the entry column never auto-advances, a second screening stage gets no rule at all, and the preview promises a landing stage ('Screened', 'Interview') that the commit does not use. Stamp each snapshot entry with its `stageRole` and `advanceTo` (the axis's next stage) in automation-pass.ts, and make evaluate_entry decide per role - with the shipped name->role map as the fallback, so the default board's decisions are byte-identical.

## Description
Everything else in the pipeline already resolves by role (stageForRole, screeningGateIndex, the aging tier), and the registry law is explicit: automated actions are permitted per role, so a new stage inherits a defined answer rather than an accident. The policy pass is the one rule engine still keyed on labels, and it fails silently - `no policy for this stage` is a valid output. The move: (1) `withPolicyStageFacts(entries, axisFor)` in automation-pass.ts adds `stageRole = roleOf(stage, axis)` and `advanceTo = nextStageOnAxis(stage, axis)` (or null) to each entry before entries.json is written; (2) evaluate_entry reads `stageRole` (falling back to DEFAULT_STAGE_ROLE[stage] when the key is absent), applies the entry rule at `entry`, the score/fairness rules at `screening`, holds at homework/scoring/custom/interview/offer, answers none at terminal and at an off-axis (null) role, and returns `advanceTo` as toStage; (3) a sync test pins the Python map and vocabulary to pipeline-stages.ts. The adverse path does not widen in kind: a reject is still only BAU + genuine score < 40, still queued for a human (automation-pass.ts retired AUTO1), and the fairness backstop is unchanged. Read->write strategy: unchanged and named - the snapshot is read-only, and every apply already goes through actOnPipelineEntry with the `expectedStage` + `expectedApprovalKind` compare-and-swap (automation-pass.ts:468). Perf: no new module - the helper lives in automation-pass.ts and uses pipeline-axis-server / pipeline-stages / db/pipeline-core, which are already on its graph via automation-run.ts; the task-hub graph gains nothing.

## Flow
1. Write the eight acceptance cases (Python unittest in test_automation.py, node:test in the new automation-pass-stage-facts.test.ts) - all red.
2. Add DEFAULT_STAGE_ROLE + the role vocabulary to automation.py; rewrite evaluate_entry's stage switch as a role switch that reads `advanceTo`; keep POLICY thresholds and reason wording (with the target stage substituted).
3. Add and export `withPolicyStageFacts` in automation-pass.ts; call it on the snapshot before writing entries.json (dry run and commit share it).
4. Add the sync test beside AgingTierSyncTest.
5. Update docs/features/pipeline/README.md (policy pass step 2) and docs/features/compliance/ai-act-conformity.md (the reject path is 'a screening-role stage', not the literal Screened).
6. Gates: tsc, lint, test:unit, test:python:gate, docs:check.

## Expected impact
A team that edits its board in Settings -> Hiring keeps its automation: arrivals with a score clear their entry column, every screening-role stage gets the same thresholds, human-owned stages hold explicitly, and the preview's planned stage is the stage the commit lands on. On the shipped board nothing moves. It also closes the last label-keyed rule engine, so a future stage-role addition is an exhaustive-branch change rather than a silent gap.

## Evaluation
Claim: the policy pass decides by stage role and names the axis's own next stage, with default-board decisions unchanged.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - Python unittest cases on evaluate_entry plus the TS-source sync test (test:python:gate), and node:test cases on withPolicyStageFacts (test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
